sections.html:
Columbus County deeds go to Suite B at 125 Washington Street, Whiteville. Mail goes to PO Box 1086, Whiteville, 28472. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and shuts for county holidays.

New recordings are taken until 4:45 p.m. each day, a quarter hour ahead of closing time. Marriage license applications end at 4:30 p.m.

Sellers reach this office last. Both your deed to the buyer and the buyer's lender's deed of trust are filed in Whiteville, typically by the closing attorney or title office. Keep the cutoff in mind when you read a closing calendar.

Ordinary deeds start at $26.00 for fifteen pages and add $4.00 per extra page. Columbus follows the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10.

Columbus County recording fees
DocumentFee
Deed of trust$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, plus $4.00 per added page
Deeds, easements and most other instruments$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, plus $4.00 per added page
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo charge
  • Seller pays nothing to record a release of a paid-off mortgage. Certified copies cost $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each page after, and a UCC filing for two pages is $38.00.
  • Copies made at the counter or ordered by mail cost 25 cents a page, and online viewing of deeds is free.
  • A notary oath taken at the office carries a $10 fee, payable by cash or local check.

Whoever sells pays the excise tax, and it is collected at the counter ahead of filing. The rate in G.S. 105-228.30 is $1 per $500 of price or value, with any part of $500 rounded up. The county FAQ gives the same rate as $2 per thousand dollars of purchase price. One half stays in the county, and the state revenue department gets the other.

The amount rises with the price and appears as its own settlement line. Register staff cannot quote it without the deed in front of them, so get the number from your closing attorney before signing day.

To change the name on title, record a new deed at the usual $26.00 rate. The office advises hiring an attorney to draft it and warns that excise tax can apply.

Electronic recording covers every document type but plats. The register's website lists the approved vendors on its e-recording page. A closing package filed that way can make the 4:45 p.m. cutoff with nobody driving to Whiteville.

The online index works by name, so each search begins with a person or company rather than a house number, and staff cannot say who owns a given street address. If you need to find an owner by address, the county tax office is the place; its land records and mapping staff can help.

  • Enter the owner's name, then open the recorded deed.
  • Compare the legal description in the deed against your tax bill.
  • Scan the deed of trust section for a mortgage that never got a satisfaction.
  • Questions about mechanics liens and judgments belong with the Clerk of Court at the courthouse, not the register.

When two claims compete for one piece of land, the recording date settles it. Registration is what counts under G.S. 47-18. Until a deed, option, long lease or right of first refusal is registered in the land's county, its holder has no shield against lien creditors or paying buyers, and the first to register ranks highest. A signed deed alone does not finish a sale, because until the register stamps a recording time on it, a later claim could still move ahead.

Owner financing is a special case under Chapter 47H, which covers a home for one to four families sold in five or more payments while the seller retains title. The seller must file the contract or a memorandum within five business days, and the buyer can cancel for three business days. Study the whole chapter first.

A parcel near active farming picks up a warning in the land records under Session Law 2018-113. The triggers are a qualifying poultry, swine or dairy farm, or a voluntary agricultural district, within one-half mile, or any other qualifying farm within 600 feet.

Your buyer's title search may flag the parcel. Nobody can sue over a researcher's failure to report the notice, and brokers and appraisers are not liable for omitting it. It informs; it does not restrict the sale. About 54 people live per square mile on the county's 938.12 square miles of land, which makes farm neighbors common. Buyers will ask about it, so have an answer ready.

If you file the deed without a closing attorney, check the basics before you drive to Whiteville. Count your pages so you can bring the exact fee, which is paid when you file. Know the excise tax figure beforehand, because staff cannot calculate it without the deed. Get there before the 4:45 p.m. intake cutoff, and let an attorney draft the document, as the office advises.

Once recorded, the deed can be viewed online at no charge, or you can ask for a certified copy at the counter.

Think of the recording step as the last domino. Once the buyer's funds are cleared and everyone has signed, the closing attorney sends the deed and the lender's deed of trust to Suite B, either by hand or through an e-recording vendor. If the package misses the 4:45 p.m. window, nothing is wrong with the sale; it simply sits until the next business morning, and a competing claim that gets registered first would outrank yours.

A seller who is out of town should confirm that the deed was recorded and not just signed. A quick look at the name-based online index will show it.

Columbus is rural, with about 50,487 residents and 23,724 housing units. Owner-occupants live in 71.1% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $146,000. Just 55 building permits were issued in 2025, so almost every deed moves an older house. Weigh your asking price against that median.

sections.h2: What the county tax bill means for closing
sections.html:
Taxes come due September 1. The tax office accepts mail (PO Box 1468, Whiteville), phone, drop box, counter and online payment at columbus.webtaxpay.com.

No penalty applies until early January. Then comes a 2% charge for January 6 to the end of that month, followed by three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of a month beginning February 1 (G.S. 105-360). The tax lien on real property attaches as of the listing date, so an unpaid bill stays with the parcel when it sells.

Before you close, ask the tax office for the amount owed and pass that payoff figure to whoever prepares your settlement statement. The assessor handles homestead relief for seniors and disabled owners on Form AV-9 and can supply current forms. If back taxes or repairs make an ordinary sale hard, a cash sale is another route; see our North Carolina page.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Columbus County sale?
faqs.a: The register's office in Whiteville. Your closing attorney or title office normally submits the package, at the counter or through an e-recording vendor, before the 4:45 p.m. intake cutoff.

faqs.q: What does the register charge for a deed here?
faqs.a: A flat $26.00 covers fifteen pages, and each added page is $4.00. A deed of trust runs $64.00 for 35 pages.

faqs.q: Who owes the deed excise tax on a Columbus County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The register collects at the counter before filing, at one dollar per $500 of price or value, which the county FAQ words as $2 per thousand dollars.

faqs.q: Can the Register of Deeds look up who owns a certain address?
faqs.a: No. The retrieval system is name based, so a search needs a person or company name. Use the county tax office for address-based parcel records.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about liens and judgments on a Columbus County property?
faqs.a: Ask the Clerk of Court at the courthouse. Also check recorded deeds of trust for any unreleased mortgage.
